relevance_reason: Treatment series of LC-FAOD patients, including LCHAD deficiency, given triheptanoin. It supports clinical management but does not break out results for LCHAD patients specifically.

findings.statement: Guffon et al. (2021) retrospectively studied 18 French patients (8 female, 10 male) with long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders (VLCAD, LCHAD, CACT, CPTII, and MTP deficiencies). The patients received triheptanoin through early access for a median of 22 months (range, 9-228 months), and at last consultation it supplied 15 to 35% of daily calories. In the year after starting triheptanoin, patients reported less intermittent snacking and fewer nocturnal meals. Three patients no longer had severe hypoglycemic events. Ten of 12 pediatric and 4 of 6 adult patients reported less fatigue and fewer, less severe episodes of myalgia. Five of the 6 patients who had needed a wheelchair no longer needed it. Emergency hospitalizations decreased, with none in pediatric patients, and annual days of emergency home care fell from 286 to 51. Adverse events were limited to digestive problems that resolved over time. The authors suggested that long-term triheptanoin is safe and markedly improves symptoms and quality of life.
quotes: Eight female and 10 male patients with LC-FAOD (VLCAD, LCHAD, CACT, CPTII and MTP) were treated with triheptanoin for a median duration of 22 months (range: 9-228 months).
Ten of 12 paediatric patients and 4 of 6 adult patients reported reduced fatigue with reductions in the number and severity of episodes of myalgia.
Cumulative annual days of emergency care in the home were reduced from 286 to 51 days in the year before and after initiation, respectively, and 13 patients required no such interventions.

relevance_reason: Reports plasma acylcarnitine responses to fasting, feeding and exercise in 11 treated patients with LCHAD/TFP deficiency, together with their genotypes and a genotype-biomarker comparison.

findings.statement: Elizondo et al. (2020) measured plasma acylcarnitines in 11 treated patients with LCHAD/TFP deficiency who were on a controlled low long-chain-fat diet with MCT. After a 10-hour overnight fast, C18:1-OH was the most prominent long-chain acylcarnitine (0.56 +/- 0.52 umol/L; reference 0.00-0.05). C16-OH and C18-OH were also above the reference range. C18:1-OH fell by 59% after breakfast and rose by only 20% after 45 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise, a response that was fairly consistent across subjects.
quotes: The most prominent fasting long-chain acylcarnitine was C18:1-OH (0.56 ± 0.52 μmol/L; reference range of 0.00–0.05 μmol/L) (Figure 3A). C16-OH and C18-OH were higher than the reference range (0.00 – 0.05 μmol/L and 0.00 – 0.02 μmol/L, respectively).
Unlike the exercise response with CPT2D and VLCADD, this hydroxyacylcarnitine species did not increase much after exercise (20%) and was relatively consistent across subjects (Figure 3C).

findings.statement: Elizondo et al. (2020) found that the newborn-screening discriminating ratios for LCHAD deficiency, C16-OH/C16 and C18-OH/C18, stayed elevated in treated patients. They concluded that disease-specific acylcarnitines vary widely through the day with feeding, fasting and activity. They therefore recommended that blood for plasma acylcarnitine analysis be collected under standardized conditions, timed in relation to food intake and physical activity.
quotes: two acylcarnitine ratios are used to improve diagnostic discrimination of LCHADD in NBS: C16-OH/C16 and C18-OH/C18. These ratios were elevated despite treatment when compared to NBS normal ranges (Supplemental Table 1).
it is recommended that standardized procedures for sample collection (i.e., timing in relation to food intake and physical activity) are strictly followed to improve their clinical interpretation.

findings.statement: Elizondo et al. (2020) reported that 9 of 11 patients with LCHAD/TFP deficiency were either homozygous or compound heterozygous for the common HADHA variant c.1528G>C (E510Q). Two patients did not carry it. One was a female with c.901G>A (G301S) and an unidentified second allele. The other was a male compound heterozygous for c.1150-1G>T and c.208T>C (S70P). These variants had previously been reported as pathogenic and associated with a TFP deficiency phenotype.
quotes: Nine of these eleven participants were either homozygous or compound heterozygous for the common pathogenic HADHA variant c.1528G>C.

Two subjects did not carry the common mutation: a female with a c.901G>A/? genotype and a male with a compound heterozygous genotype (c.1150-1G>1/c.208T>C). These mutations were previously reported as pathogenic variants associated with a TFP deficiency phenotype.

findings.statement: Elizondo et al. (2020) found that the 9 patients carrying the common c.1528G>C variant on at least one HADHA allele had consistently higher C16-OH, C18-OH and C18:1-OH levels than the 2 patients without it, who had a TFP deficiency phenotype. Mean fasting C18:0-OH was 0.229 umol/L in carriers versus 0.016 umol/L in non-carriers, but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.09). The authors suggested that variants which destabilize the protein and abolish mitochondrial TFP expression produce low hydroxyacylcarnitine levels because hydratase activity is absent, so the acylcarnitine profile more closely resembles that of VLCAD deficiency.
quotes: Nine out of the 11 subjects had at least one allele with the common mutation (c.1528G>C; LCHADD) with a fasting C18:0-OH mean of 0.229 μmol/L. The 2 subjects without the common mutation (TFPD) are graphed in red and are on the low end on the spectrum with a fasting C18-OH mean of 0.016 μmol/L.

These findings suggest that mutations that destabilize the protein and result in a loss of mitochondrial TFP expression have low OH-species due to the absence of the hydratase activity. Thus, the plasma acylcarnitine profile will more closely resemble that of a patient with VLCADD.

findings.statement: Elizondo et al. (2020) found that across 30 treated patients with long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders, including LCHAD deficiency, feeding consistently suppressed disease-specific acylcarnitines by about 60%. Fasting plasma free fatty acids correlated with the fasting sum of long-chain acylcarnitines. The authors concluded that this supports fasting avoidance and frequent meals. All patients tolerated moderate exercise, which the authors said supported current recommendations for patients to be physically active.
quotes: Feeding suppresses lipolysis and plasma LC-acylcarnitines (Figure 4A and 4B), supporting the role of fasting avoidance and frequent meals for lowering LC-acylcarnitines in patients with LC-FAODs.
All patients tolerated the exercise further supporting the current recommendations for patients with FAODs to be physically active which could improve long-term fitness and exercise tolerance.

relevance_reason: Case report of LCHAD deficiency caused by homozygosity for the common HADHA E510Q mutation, which arose through paternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 2.

findings.statement: Baskin et al. (2010) reported a 22-month-old child with LCHAD deficiency who was identified on expanded newborn screening by an abnormal acylcarnitine pattern with increased C14OH.
quotes: We report on a 22-month-old child who was identified on expanded newborn screening with an abnormal acylcarnitine pattern and increased C14OH.

phenotypes.text: abnormal acylcarnitine pattern with increased C14OH

findings.statement: Baskin et al. (2010) found that a child with LCHAD deficiency was homozygous for the common HADHA mutation c.1526G>C (p.Glu510Gln). The father was heterozygous for the mutation, but the mother did not carry it. Short tandem repeat testing with markers covering both the short and long arms of chromosome 2 showed that the child had paternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 2.
quotes: Molecular analysis showed that the child was homozygous for the common mutation, c.1526G > C (p.Glu510Gln) in the HADHA gene.
Carrier testing on the parental samples revealed that the father was heterozygous for the mutation whereas the mother did not carry the mutation.
Short tandem repeat testing with markers covering both short and long arms of chromosome 2 showed that the child has paternal uniparental isodisomy.

findings.statement: Baskin et al. (2010) showed by short tandem repeat analysis that homozygosity for an HADHA mutation in a child with LCHAD deficiency resulted from paternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 2. They emphasized the importance of parental testing when a patient with an autosomal recessive disorder is homozygous, because of its impact on genetic counseling.
quotes: Short tandem repeat testing with markers covering both short and long arms of chromosome 2 showed that the child has paternal uniparental isodisomy.
We highlight the importance of parental testing in cases of homozygosity in autosomal recessive disorders and its impact on genetic counseling of the family.

relevance_reason: In vitro fibroblast study of LCHAD/MTP-deficient cells examining effect of medium-chain fatty acids on 3-hydroxy-fatty acid accumulation, relevant to dietary management of LCHAD deficiency.

findings.statement: Jones et al. (2003) used an in vitro model to study the effects of dietary treatment in LCHAD deficiency. They grew cultured skin fibroblasts from LCHAD-deficient and normal individuals in media supplemented with physiologic combinations of the medium-chain fatty acids octanoate and decanoate and the long-chain fatty acid palmitate, and measured 3-hydroxy-fatty acids in the medium by stable-isotope dilution gas chromatography/mass spectrometry. Addition of medium-chain fatty acids decreased the accumulation of long-chain fatty acid oxidation intermediates in LCHAD-deficient cells, both in untreated medium and with added palmitate, and decanoate alone was more effective than octanoate alone.
quotes: We found that the addition of medium-chain fatty acids caused a decrease in the accumulation of long-chain fatty acid oxidation intermediates in LCHAD-deficient cells when the cells were incubated in untreated medium, and also when they were incubated in this medium with palmitate added.
Medium with decanoate alone was better at achieving this effect than medium with only octanoate added.

findings.statement: Jones et al. (2003) found that a 1:3 ratio of octanoate to decanoate worked best over an extended time in LCHAD-deficient fibroblasts in untreated medium, whereas a 1:1 ratio worked best in medium containing palmitate. Because all dietary medium-chain triglyceride preparations contain more octanoate than decanoate, the authors suggested that a preparation higher in decanoate may be more effective in reducing the accumulation of potentially toxic long-chain 3-hydroxy-fatty acids in LCHAD deficiency.
quotes: A 1:3 ratio of octanoate to decanoate worked best over an extended time period in LCHAD-deficient cells in untreated medium, whereas a 1:1 ratio of octanoate to decanoate worked best in the same cells incubated in medium containing palmitate.

Our results suggest that a medium-chain triglyceride preparation that is higher in decanoate may be more effective in reducing the accumulation of potentially toxic long-chain 3-hydroxy-fatty acids in LCHAD deficiency.

relevance_reason: Functional study showing mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, LCHAD activity and MTP expression in the retinal pigment epithelium. This bears on how pigmentary retinopathy arises in LCHAD deficiency.

findings.statement: To study how pigmentary retinopathy arises in LCHAD deficiency, Tyni et al. (2002) cultured porcine retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells. These cells shortened [U-13C]-hexadecanoic acid normally and produced acetylcarnitine. They also had LCHAD enzyme activity, expressed the mitochondrial trifunctional protein (MTP) and could take up carnitine. In human retinal sections, MTP antibodies labeled the RPE, photoreceptors and ganglion cells. The authors concluded that this was strong in vitro evidence for mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation in the RPE. They noted that further studies were needed to clarify whether the pathway also acts in the retina in vivo.
quotes: Fatty acid oxidation analysis showed normal chain shortening of hexadecanoic acid and production of acetylcarnitine in cultured RPE cells. Immunoblotting revealed expression of the MTP and enzyme assay showed the activity of LCHAD in the RPE cells. RPE cells were also capable of carnitine uptake.
Positive labeling to the MTP antibodies was detected in the RPE, photoreceptors, and ganglion cells.
The results give strong in vitro evidence for the presence of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation in RPE cells and the expression of the MTP in the RPE and other layers of the retina.

relevance_reason: Large cohort study (50 patients) describing clinical presentation, course, mortality and morbidity of LCHAD deficiency.

findings.statement: den Boer et al. (2002) reviewed questionnaire data on 50 of 61 unselected patients with LCHAD deficiency diagnosed at their center. The mean age at clinical presentation was 5.8 months (range, 1 day to 26 months), and 7 (15%) presented in the neonatal period. Thirty-nine patients (78%) presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, whereas 11 (22%) presented with chronic problems consisting of failure to thrive, feeding difficulties, cholestatic liver disease, and/or hypotonia.
quotes: The mean age of clinical presentation was 5.8 months (range: 1 day-26 months). Seven (15%) of the patients presented in the neonatal period.
Thirty-nine patients (78%) presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, the classical features of a fatty acid oxidation disorder.
Eleven patients (22%) presented with chronic problems, consisting of failure to thrive, feeding difficulties, cholestatic liver disease, and/or hypotonia.

findings.statement: den Boer et al. (2002) found that, in retrospect, 82% of the patients who presented with an acute metabolic derangement had also had a combination of chronic nonspecific symptoms before the metabolic crises, and concluded that LCHAD deficiency often presents with chronic nonspecific symptoms, making early diagnosis difficult in the absence of the classical metabolic derangement.
quotes: In retrospect, most (82%) of the patients presenting with an acute metabolic derangement also suffered from a combination of chronic nonspecific symptoms before the metabolic crises.
LCHAD deficiency often presents with a combination of chronic nonspecific symptoms. Early diagnosis is difficult in the absence of the classical metabolic derangement.

findings.statement: den Boer et al. (2002) reported high mortality (38%) in their series of 50 LCHAD-deficient patients, all deaths occurring before or within 3 months after diagnosis. Morbidity among survivors was also high, with recurrent metabolic crises and muscle problems despite therapy.
quotes: Mortality in this series was high (38%), all dying before or within 3 months after diagnosis.
Morbidity in the surviving patients is also high, with recurrent metabolic crises and muscle problems despite therapy.

findings.statement: den Boer et al. (2002) concluded that survival in LCHAD deficiency can be improved by prompt diagnosis but that morbidity remains alarmingly high despite current therapeutic regimens.
quotes: Survival can be improved by prompt diagnosis, but morbidity remains alarmingly high despite current therapeutic regimes.

findings.statement: den Boer et al. (2002) described LCHAD deficiency as a rare autosomal recessive inborn error of fatty acid oxidation.
quotes: LCHAD deficiency is a rare, autosomal recessive inborn error of fatty acid oxidation.

relevance_reason: Reports molecular prenatal diagnosis in families with LCHAD deficiency and complete TFP deficiency, plus outcomes of heterozygous-mother pregnancies (relevant to maternal pregnancy complications).

findings.statement: Ibdah et al. (2001) performed molecular prenatal diagnosis in 9 pregnancies: 8 in 6 families with isolated LCHAD deficiency and 1 in a family with complete mitochondrial trifunctional protein (TFP) deficiency, using chorionic villus samples in 7 and amniocytes in 2. The fetal genotype was identified in all 9 pregnancies; 2 fetuses were affected (pregnancies terminated), 2 had a normal genotype, and 5 were heterozygotes. Genotypes were confirmed by molecular analysis and enzymatic assays in the aborted fetuses and neonates, and the authors concluded that molecular prenatal diagnosis is possible and valid in families with known TFP defects.
quotes: We performed molecular prenatal diagnosis in 9 pregnancies, 8 in 6 families with isolated long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency and one in a family with complete TFP deficiency.
Molecular prenatal diagnosis successfully identified the fetal genotype in all 9 pregnancies. Two fetuses were affected, and both pregnancies were terminated by family decision.
Genotypes of the aborted fetuses and neonates were confirmed by molecular analysis and enzymatic assays.

findings.statement: Ibdah et al. (2001) found that the 7 pregnancies in which women heterozygous for TFP alpha-subunit mutations carried fetuses with wild-type or heterozygous genotypes were uncomplicated, and all offspring were alive and apparently healthy.
quotes: Two other fetuses had normal genotype and 5 others were heterozygotes. These 7 pregnancies were uncomplicated, and all the offspring are alive and apparently healthy.
Women heterozygous for TFP alpha-subunit mutations who carry fetuses with wild-type or heterozygous genotypes have uncomplicated pregnancies.

relevance_reason: Characterizes the acylcarnitine profiles in plasma and blood spots of 23 LCHAD-deficient patients. Gives diagnostic criteria and shows that diet therapy lowers the markers, so the assay can be used to monitor treatment.

findings.statement: Van Hove et al. (2000) reviewed the acylcarnitines in plasma and blood spots of 23 patients with proven LCHAD deficiency. The long-chain 3-hydroxyacylcarnitines C14:1, C14, C16 and C18:1 were elevated, as were the long-chain acylcarnitines C12, C14:1, C14, C16, C18:2 and C18:1. Acetylcarnitine was decreased.
quotes: The acylcarnitines in plasma and blood spots of 23 patients with proven deficiency of long-chain 3-hydroxyacylcoenzyme A dehydrogenase were reviewed.

Long-chain 3-hydroxyacylcarnitines of C14:1, C14, C16 and C18:1 chain length, and long-chain acylcarnitines of C12, C14:1, C14, C16, C18:2 and C18:1 chain length were elevated. Acetylcarnitine was decreased.

findings.statement: Van Hove et al. (2000) found that, in plasma, hydroxy-C18:1 acylcarnitine above the 95th centile of controls, combined with elevation of two of the three acylcarnitines C14, C14:1 and hydroxy-C16, identified over 85% of LCHAD-deficient patients with a false-positive rate below 0.1%. Diagnostic specificity was lower in blood spots than in plasma because normal erythrocytes contain high endogenous levels of long-chain acylcarnitines. The profile was also diagnostic in asymptomatic patients and was not influenced by genotype.
quotes: In plasma, elevation of hydroxy-C18:1 acylcarnitine over the 95th centile of controls, in combination with an elevation of two of the three acylcarnitines C14, C14:1 and hydroxy-C16, identified over 85% of patients with high specificity (less than 0.1% false positive rate).
High endogenous levels of long-chain acylcarnitines in normal erythrocytes reduced the diagnostic specificity in blood spots compared with plasma samples.
The results were also diagnostic in asymptomatic patients, and were not influenced by genotype.

findings.statement: Van Hove et al. (2000) found that a diet low in fat and high in medium-chain triglyceride lowered all disease-specific acylcarnitines in LCHAD-deficient patients, often to normal levels. They suggested that the assay is useful for monitoring treatment.
quotes: Treatment with diet low in fat and high in medium-chain triglyceride decreased all disease-specific acylcarnitines, often to normal, suggesting that this assay is useful in treatment monitoring.

relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It reports a neonatal diagnosis of LCHAD deficiency and discusses what this means for newborn screening by tandem mass spectrometry, which is relevant to the diagnosis section of the entry.

findings.statement: Carpenter and Wilcken (1999) reported a neonatal diagnosis of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency and discussed what it means for newborn screening by tandem mass spectrometry.
quotes: Neonatal diagnosis of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency and implications for newborn screening by tandem mass spectrometry.

relevance_reason: Case report of LCHAD deficiency that presented on the first day of life with tachypnea. Only the title was available, so the details cannot be checked.

findings.statement: Thiel et al. (1999) reported long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency that showed itself in the newborn period on the first day of life, presenting with tachypnea.
quotes: Long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: neonatal manifestation at the first day of life presenting with tachypnoea.

relevance_reason: Case report of an LCHAD-deficient infant who was homozygous for E474Q and had an unusual presentation. The mother developed pregnancy complications.

findings.statement: Ibdah et al. (1999) described an infant with LCHAD deficiency that had not been suspected. At 2 months of age the infant presented with acute infantile hypocalcemia and vitamin D deficiency, together with occult, unexplained cholestatic liver disease. The infant died suddenly and unexpectedly at 8 months. The authors concluded that infantile hypocalcemia is an unusual phenotype associated with LCHAD deficiency.
quotes: The proband presented at 2 months of age with an acute infantile hypocalcaemia and vitamin D deficiency associated with occult, unexplained cholestatic liver disease. Sudden, unexpected death occurred at 8 months.
In conclusion, infantile hypocalcaemia is an unusual phenotype associated with LCHAD deficiency.

findings.statement: In the infant with LCHAD deficiency who presented with hypocalcemia and cholestasis, Ibdah et al. (1999) found by molecular analysis that the infant was homozygous for the common LCHAD mutation 1528G-C (E474Q).
quotes: Molecular analysis revealed homozygosity for the prevalent LCHAD (1528G > C, E474Q) mutation.

findings.statement: Ibdah et al. (1999) reported that the mother of the LCHAD-deficient infant had preeclampsia in the third trimester of that pregnancy. In a later pregnancy she developed severe acute fatty liver of pregnancy (AFLP), and the fetus died in utero at 33 weeks' gestation. The authors concluded that fetal LCHAD deficiency is associated with a range of maternal illnesses, from preeclampsia to life-threatening AFLP.
quotes: The mother had pre-eclampsia during the third trimester of her pregnancy. In a subsequent pregnancy, she developed severe acute fatty liver of pregnancy (AFLP) and intrauterine fetal death at 33 weeks of gestation.
fetal LCHAD deficiency is associated with a spectrum of maternal illnesses ranging from pre-eclampsia to life-threatening AFLP.

relevance_reason: The study reports HADHA mutations, including the common Glu474Gln mutation, in children with isolated LCHAD deficiency, and links fetal LCHAD deficiency to maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy and HELLP syndrome.

findings.statement: Ibdah et al. (1999) studied 24 children with 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. Nineteen had a deficiency only of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia and fatty liver.
quotes: Nineteen children had a deficiency only of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia and fatty liver.

findings.statement: Ibdah et al. (1999) used DNA amplification and nucleotide-sequence analysis of the alpha subunit of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein in children with isolated LCHAD deficiency. Eight children were homozygous for a glu474-to-gln (E474Q) mutation. Eleven others were compound heterozygous for this mutation and a different mutation on the other allele.
quotes: In eight children, we identified a homozygous mutation in which glutamic acid at residue 474 was changed to glutamine.
Eleven other children were compound heterozygotes, with this mutation in one allele of the alpha-subunit gene and a different mutation in the other allele.

findings.statement: Ibdah et al. (1999) found that 79% of heterozygous mothers had acute fatty liver of pregnancy or HELLP syndrome while carrying fetuses with the Glu474Gln mutation. The authors concluded that women with acute liver disease during pregnancy may have the Glu474Gln mutation, and that their infants are at risk for hypoketotic hypoglycemia and fatty liver.
quotes: While carrying fetuses with the Glu474Gln mutation, 79 percent of the heterozygous mothers had fatty liver of pregnancy or the HELLP syndrome.
Women with acute liver disease during pregnancy may have a Glu474Gln mutation in long-chain hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase. Their infants are at risk for hypoketotic hypoglycemia and fatty liver.

phenotypes.text: maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy

findings.statement: Ibdah et al. (1999) described 5 other children with complete trifunctional protein deficiency, meaning loss of activity of all 3 enzymes. These children presented with neonatal dilated cardiomyopathy or progressive neuromyopathy. None had the Glu474Gln mutation, and none of their mothers had liver disease during pregnancy.
quotes: Five other children, who presented with neonatal dilated cardiomyopathy or progressive neuromyopathy, had complete deficiency of the trifunctional protein (loss of activity of all three enzymes). None had the Glu474Gln mutation, and none of their mothers had liver disease during pregnancy.

relevance_reason: Case report of two patients with L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency who had pigmentary retinopathy. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Uusimaa et al. (1997) reported 2 patients with L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency who had pigmentary retinopathy.
quotes: L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency: two cases with pigmentary retinopathy.

relevance_reason: This is a case report of 2 patients with LCHAD deficiency. It describes the retinal dystrophy seen in the disorder.

findings.statement: Schrijver-Wieling et al. (1997) reported 2 girls with LCHAD deficiency, aged 8 and 15 years. Both had extensive macular pigment deposits and a 'salt and pepper' scattering of pigment in the retina, and both had decreasing visual acuity.
quotes: The case histories of two girls, aged 8 and 15 years, with LCHAD deficiency are reported.
Both children with LCHAD deficiency exhibited extensive macular pigmentary depositions and a 'salt and pepper' scattering of pigment in their retinas. The patients have decreasing visual acuity.

findings.statement: Schrijver-Wieling et al. (1997) noted that LCHAD deficiency, a defect of fatty acid breakdown, is associated with life-threatening episodes of hypoketotic hypoglycemia during prolonged fasting. They also noted that neuropathy and retinal pigment changes had been mentioned in only a few cases.
quotes: A deficiency of this enzyme is associated with life threatening episodes of hypoketotic hypoglycaemia during prolonged fasting. Neuropathy and retinopigmentary changes were mentioned in only a few cases.

findings.statement: Schrijver-Wieling et al. (1997) noted that patients tend to have no symptoms between attacks. They recommended that testing for LCHAD deficiency be included in the workup of children with retinal dystrophy, especially when other clinical symptoms have occurred. They said early recognition could increase life expectancy by avoiding catabolism and by using appropriate diets.
quotes: Patients tend to be free of symptoms between attacks, however. Testing for the disorder, therefore, should be included in the diagnostic process for children with retinal dystrophy, in particular when other clinical symptoms are known to have occurred.
The early recognition of LCHAD deficiency can increase the life expectancy in these patients through avoiding catabolism and through appropriate diets.

relevance_reason: Clinical series of 13 LCHAD-deficient patients, all homozygous for the common G1528C mutation.

findings.statement: Tyni et al. (1997) reported the clinical findings in 13 patients with LCHAD deficiency. At presentation, during the first 2 years of life, the patients had hypoglycemia, cardiomyopathy, muscle hypotonia, and hepatomegaly. Seven patients had recurrent metabolic crises and 6 had a steadily progressive course. Two patients had cholestatic liver disease, which the authors noted is uncommon in beta-oxidation defects; 1 had peripheral neuropathy; and 6 had retinopathy with focal pigmentary aggregations or retinal hypopigmentation.
quotes: At presentation the patients had had hypoglycemia, cardiomyopathy, muscle hypotonia, and hepatomegaly during the first 2 years of life. Seven patients had recurrent metabolic crises, and six patients had a steadily progressive course.

Two patients had cholestatic liver disease, which is uncommon in beta-oxidation defects. One patient had peripheral neuropathy, and six patients had retinopathy with focal pigmentary aggregations or retinal hypopigmentation.

phenotypes.text: retinopathy with focal pigmentary aggregations or retinal hypopigmentation

findings.statement: Tyni et al. (1997) found dicarboxylic aciduria in 9 of 10 patients with LCHAD deficiency tested, and most patients had lactic acidosis, increased serum creatine kinase activity, and low serum carnitine concentration. Enoyl-CoA hydratase and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activities of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein were variably decreased in skin fibroblasts.
quotes: Dicarboxylic aciduria was detected in 9 of 10 patients, and most patients had lactic acidosis, increased serum creatine kinase activities, and low serum carnitine concentration.
However, the enoyl-CoA hydratase and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activities of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein were variably decreased in skin fibroblasts.

findings.statement: Tyni et al. (1997) found bilateral periventricular or focal cortical lesions on neuroimaging in 3 of 13 patients with LCHAD deficiency and brain atrophy in 1.
quotes: Neuroradiologically there was bilateral periventricular or focal cortical lesions in three patients, and brain atrophy in one.

phenotypes.text: bilateral periventricular or focal cortical lesions

findings.statement: Tyni et al. (1997) reported that all 13 patients with LCHAD deficiency were homozygous for the common G1528C mutation.
quotes: All patients were homozygous for the common mutation G1528C.

findings.statement: Tyni et al. (1997) reported that only 1 of 13 patients with LCHAD deficiency, who had received dietary treatment for 9 years, was alive at 14 years of age; all of the others died before 2 years of age. The authors suggested that early dietary management may change the otherwise poor prognosis.
quotes: Only one patient, who has had dietary treatment for 9 years, is alive at the age of 14 years; all others died before they were 2 years of age.
Recognition of the clinical features of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA deficiency is important for the early institution of dietary management, which may alter the otherwise invariably poor prognosis.

relevance_reason: Shows through functional expression that the common HADHA G1528C mutation causes LCHAD deficiency, reports its allele frequency in patients, describes a genomic DNA test, and maps the gene.

findings.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) found the G1528C mutation in the cDNA for the alpha subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein at an allele frequency of 87% in 34 patients with LCHAD deficiency. When they expressed the wildtype and mutant proteins in S. cerevisiae, they showed that the G1528C mutation directly causes the loss of LCHAD activity.
quotes: Using S. cerevisiae for expression of wild type and mutant protein we show that the G1528C mutation is directly responsible for the loss of LCHAD activity.
The finding of an 87% allele frequency of the G1528C mutation in 34 LCHAD deficient patients makes this a valuable test for prenatal diagnosis.

findings.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) developed a method for detecting the G1528C mutation in genomic DNA. Because the mutation had an allele frequency of 87% among LCHAD-deficient patients, they suggested the test was valuable for prenatal diagnosis.
quotes: Furthermore, we describe a newly developed method allowing identification of the G1528C mutation in genomic DNA.
The finding of an 87% allele frequency of the G1528C mutation in 34 LCHAD deficient patients makes this a valuable test for prenatal diagnosis.

findings.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) showed that the gene encoding the alpha subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein is located on chromosome 2p24.1-p23.3.
quotes: Finally, we show that the gene encoding the alpha subunit of MTP is located on chromosome 2p24.1-23.3.

findings.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) noted that in most patients only the LCHAD activity of mitochondrial trifunctional protein is deficient, while its long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase and long-chain 3-ketothiolase activities are near normal. They described the deficiency as impairing oxidation of long-chain fatty acids, which can lead to sudden infant death.
quotes: In most patients only the LCHAD activity of MTP is deficient with near normal activity of the two other enzyme activities of the complex.
A deficiency of this protein is associated with impaired oxidation of long-chain fatty acids which can lead to sudden infant death.

findings.statement: IJlst et al. (1996) stated that this inborn error of fatty acid oxidation is very frequent, second only to medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency.
quotes: Furthermore, it is clear that this inborn error of fatty acid oxidation is very frequent, second to medium chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency.

relevance_reason: The paper describes an infant with LCHAD deficiency whose heterozygous mother had acute fatty liver of pregnancy, and it proposes a mechanism linking the two.

findings.statement: Treem et al. (1994) reported a full-term infant who seemed normal at birth and presented at 4 months of age with hypoglycemia, coma and profound hepatic steatosis. The infant was found to have long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. The mother had had acute fatty liver of pregnancy during this pregnancy.
quotes: We report a woman with acute fatty liver of pregnancy who gave birth to a seemingly normal full-term infant who was seen at 4 mo of age with hypoglycemia, coma and profound hepatic steatosis.

phenotypes.text: maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy

findings.statement: Treem et al. (1994) found that the mother of the LCHAD-deficient infant was heterozygous for the defect. They hypothesized that some cases of acute fatty liver of pregnancy are caused by the interaction between an affected fetus and a mother who is heterozygous for this fatty acid oxidation defect in the late third trimester.
quotes: The infant had a defect in fatty acid oxidation, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase deficiency, and the mother proved to be heterozygous for this metabolic condition.

We hypothesize that the interaction of an affected fetus with a female heterozygous for this defect in fatty acid oxidation in the late third trimester accounts for some cases of acute fatty liver of pregnancy.

phenotypes.text: acute fatty liver of pregnancy in heterozygous mother

relevance_reason: Reports maternal pregnancy complications (fatty liver, HELLP) associated with carrying a fetus with LCHAD deficiency, a key clinical feature for the entry.

findings.statement: Wilcken et al. (1993) reported 11 pregnancies in 5 mothers; 6 of the babies had LCHAD deficiency, and each of these pregnancies was complicated by features such as maternal fatty liver and HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets) syndrome. By contrast, 3 of the mothers also gave birth to unaffected babies, and these pregnancies were largely uncomplicated.
quotes: We report on eleven pregnancies in 5 mothers. 6 of the babies had long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl coenzyme A dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency, and each of the pregnancies was complicated by features such as fatty liver and HELLP (haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets) syndrome.
By contrast, 3 of the mothers also gave birth to unaffected babies, and these pregnancies were largely uncomplicated.

findings.statement: Wilcken et al. (1993) concluded that a fetus with LCHAD deficiency may have adverse effects on maternal liver function, and that maternal heterozygosity alone cannot account for these effects because the complications segregated with fetal LCHAD status.
quotes: We conclude that there may be adverse effects on maternal liver function from a fetus with LCHAD deficiency.
Heterozygosity in the mother cannot alone account for the adverse effects because of the segregation of these effects with fetal LCHAD status.

relevance_reason: Case report of LCHAD deficiency shown in fibroblasts in a boy with Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndrome features; the authors suggest LCHAD deficiency may cause the lipid myopathy in BRRS.

findings.statement: Fryburg et al. (1994) described a black boy with features of Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndrome (BRRS) who also had a defect in long-chain fatty acid oxidation, expressed in cultured skin fibroblasts as LCHAD deficiency. He also had an abnormal brain MRI and enlargement of both lower limbs. The authors postulated that LCHAD deficiency may be the cause of the lipid myopathy in BRRS.
quotes: We describe a black boy with findings of BRRS who also has a defect in long-chain fatty acid oxidation expressed in cultured skin fibroblasts as a deficiency of long-chain-L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (L-CHAD).
He also has an abnormal brain MRI and increased size of both lower limbs.
postulate that L-CHAD deficiency may be the cause of the lipid myopathy in BRRS

phenotypes.text: increased size of both lower limbs

findings.statement: Fryburg et al. (1994) showed that cultured skin fibroblasts from a boy with Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba syndrome features had a defect in long-chain fatty acid oxidation, expressed as a deficiency of long-chain L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity.
quotes: a defect in long-chain fatty acid oxidation expressed in cultured skin fibroblasts as a deficiency of long-chain-L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (L-CHAD)

phenotypes.text: deficiency of LCHAD activity in fibroblasts

relevance_reason: This is the first paper to define the molecular basis of isolated LCHAD deficiency. It reports HADHA (trifunctional protein alpha subunit) mutations in 3 families, along with maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy.

findings.statement: Sims et al. (1995) studied 3 families with LCHAD deficiency in which the children had sudden unexplained death or hypoglycemia with abnormal liver enzymes (Reye-like syndrome). In all 3 families, the mothers had acute fatty liver of pregnancy with severe complications while pregnant with the affected infants.
quotes: three families with children presenting with sudden unexplained death or hypoglycemia and abnormal liver enzymes (Reye-like syndrome)
In all families, the mothers had acute fatty liver and associated sever complications during pregnancies with the affected infants.

phenotypes.text: maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy

findings.statement: Sims et al. (1995) used SSCV analysis of the exons of the LCHAD (trifunctional protein alpha subunit) gene and found 2 affected children homozygous for a G-to-C change at nucleotide 1528 (G1528C). The change lies in the LCHAD domain and replaces glutamic acid with glutamine at residue 474 of the mature alpha subunit (E474Q).
quotes: The analysis in two affected children revealed a G to C mutation at position 1528 (G1528C) of the alpha subunit of the trifunctional protein on both alleles.
This is in the LCHAD domain and substitutes glutamine for glutamic acid at position 474 of mature alpha subunit.

findings.statement: Sims et al. (1995) found that a third child with LCHAD deficiency was compound heterozygous for the G1528C (E474Q) mutation and a C1132T mutation. The C1132T change creates a premature stop codon at residue 342.
quotes: The third child had this G1528C mutation on one allele and a different mutation (C1132T) creating a premature termination codon (residue 342) on the second allele.

findings.statement: Sims et al. (1995) concluded that mutations in the LCHAD domain of the trifunctional protein alpha subunit in affected offspring are associated with maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy. This was the first delineation of the molecular basis of isolated LCHAD deficiency.
quotes: Our results demonstrate that mutations in the LCHAD domain of the trifunctional protein alpha subunit in affected offspring are associated with maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy.
This is the initial delineation of the molecular basis of isolated LCHAD deficiency.

phenotypes.text: maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy

findings.statement: Sims et al. (1995) noted that LCHAD catalyzes the third step of mitochondrial beta-oxidation. Its activity sits on the C-terminal portion of the alpha subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein.
quotes: Long chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase [LCHAD; long-chain-(S)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA:NAD+ oxidoreductase, EC 1.1.1.211] catalyzes the third step in beta-oxidation, and this activity is present on the C-terminal portion of the alpha subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein.

relevance_reason: Case report of a patient with LCHAD deficiency, confirmed by enzyme testing in fibroblasts, with clinical and biochemical findings.

findings.statement: Sewell et al. (1994) reported a patient with long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency who presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia, hepatopathy, secondary carnitine deficiency, and increased plasma long-chain acylcarnitines. The authors noted that the disorder, newly recognized, usually has a fatal outcome, and compared their patient with those in the literature.
quotes: We present a further patient who presented with hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, hepatopathy, secondary carnitine deficiency and increased plasma long-chain acylcarnitines.
3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency is a newly recognised fatty acid oxidation disorder with a usually fatal outcome.

findings.statement: Sewell et al. (1994) found 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria in their patient, and the diagnosis of LCHAD deficiency was confirmed by studies in cultured skin fibroblasts.
quotes: 3-Hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria was present and the diagnosis confirmed in cultured skin fibroblasts.

relevance_reason: Identifies the major disease-causing mutation (G1528C) in the alpha-subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein in patients with LCHAD deficiency.

findings.statement: In patients with long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCHAD) deficiency, IJlst et al. (1994) sequenced the cDNAs encoding the alpha- and beta-subunits of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein and identified a G-to-C mutation at nucleotide 1528 (G1528C) in the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase-encoding region of the alpha subunit, resulting in a glutamate/glutamine substitution at amino acid position 510. The change creates a PstI restriction site; by RFLP analysis, 24 of 26 unrelated patients expressed only the C1528 allele and the other 2 were heterozygous. The mutation was not found in 55 control subjects.
quotes: we sequenced the cDNAs encoding the alpha- and beta-subunits which revealed one G-->C mutation at nucleotide position 1528 in the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase encoding region of the alpha-subunit
The single base change results in the substitution of a glutamate for a glutamine at amino acid position 510.

Using RFLP, we found that in 24 out of 26 unrelated patients only the C1528 was expressed. The other two patients were heterozygous for this mutation. This mutation was not found in 55 different control subjects.

variants.as_reported: G-->C mutation at nucleotide position 1528 (C1528); glutamate/glutamine substitution at amino acid position 510

findings.statement: IJlst et al. (1994) found the G1528C mutation in the alpha subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein in all 26 unrelated LCHAD-deficient patients studied (only the mutant allele expressed in 24, heterozygous in 2) and in none of 55 controls, indicating a high frequency of this mutation among patients with LCHAD deficiency.
quotes: Using RFLP, we found that in 24 out of 26 unrelated patients only the C1528 was expressed.
This indicates a high frequency for this mutation in long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficient patients.

findings.statement: IJlst et al. (1994) noted that the mitochondrial trifunctional protein, involved in mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, harbors long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, and long-chain 3-ketothiolase activities.
quotes: Mitochondrial trifunctional protein is a newly identified enzyme involved in mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation harbouring long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and long-chain 3-ketothiolase activity.

relevance_reason: Only the title was available. It links sudden infant death to long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, which is the subject of this entry, but gives no patient, biochemical or genetic details.

findings.statement: Wanders et al. (1989) reported on sudden infant death in relation to long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase. Only the title was available, so no further detail can be given.
quotes: Sudden infant death and long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase.

relevance_reason: An early clinical description of patients with 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria, a fatty acid oxidation defect consistent with LCHAD deficiency.

findings.statement: Hagenfeldt et al. (1990) described 5 patients with a suspected defect in fatty acid beta-oxidation. During acute illness, they excreted massive amounts of 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acids in the urine and accumulated 3-hydroxy fatty acids in serum. Four of the patients died of cardiomyopathy and liver insufficiency between 3 and 14 months of age. Two of the patients had older sibs who had died unexpectedly in early infancy.
quotes: We describe five patients with a suspected defect in the beta-oxidation of fatty acids characterized by a massive excretion of 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acids in the urine and accumulation of 3-hydroxy fatty acids in serum during acute illness.
Four of them died of cardiomyopathy and liver insufficiency at 3 to 14 months of age.
Two of the patients had elder siblings who had died unexpectedly in early infancy.

findings.statement: Hagenfeldt et al. (1990) found normal long-chain and medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase activities in fibroblasts from all 5 patients with 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria. They concluded that these patients differed from previously described patients with beta-oxidation defects.
quotes: Long-chain and medium-chain acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenases in fibroblasts were normal in all patients.
These patients differ from previously described patients with beta-oxidation defects.

phenotypes.text: accumulation of 3-hydroxy fatty acids in serum

relevance_reason: Describes a patient with LCHAD deficiency demonstrated in fibroblasts, with clinical, urinary organic acid and enzymatic findings.

findings.statement: Rocchiccioli et al. (1990) described a child who presented in early childhood with episodes of coma and hypoglycemia and a rapidly progressive myopathy and cardiomyopathy, leading to death at 9 months of age. Ketosis was decreased (blood beta-hydroxybutyrate 0.07 mmol/L) even though plasma fatty acid levels were normal (0.81 mmol/L).
quotes: A child presented in early childhood with episodes of coma and hypoglycemia and a rapidly evolutive myopathy and cardiomyopathy leading to death at 9 mo of age.
Ketosis was decreased (blood beta-hydroxybutyrate: 0.07 mmol/L) despite normal plasma levels of fatty acids (0.81 mmol/L).

findings.statement: Rocchiccioli et al. (1990) found that the patient's urine contained excessive C6 to C10 dicarboxylic acids and, by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, an accumulation of medium- and long-chain (C8 to C14) 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acids, suggesting a defect of the mitochondrial enzyme that dehydrogenates 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA esters.
quotes: The patient's urine contained excessive amounts of the C6 to C10 dicarboxylic acids present in almost all defects of fatty acid mitochondrial oxidation.

gas chromatography-mass spectrometry identified an accumulation of medium- and long-chain (C8 to C14) 3-hydroxy-dicarboxylic acids, suggesting a defect of the mitochondrial enzyme that normally dehydrogenates these 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA esters.

findings.statement: Rocchiccioli et al. (1990) showed impaired medium- and long-chain fatty acid oxidation in the patient's cultured fibroblasts and identified deficiency of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase; activities of long-, medium-, and short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenases and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase were normal. They concluded that the disorder affects liver, skeletal muscle, and myocardium.
quotes: Biochemical studies in the patient's cultured fibroblasts confirmed the impairment of medium- and long-chain fatty acid oxidation, and allowed the recognition of the deficiency of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
The activities of long-, medium-, and short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenases and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase were normal.
These results describe a disorder of fatty acid metabolism that affects the liver, skeletal muscles, and myocardium.

findings.statement: Rocchiccioli et al. (1990) noted that LCHAD deficiency shares many clinical similarities with systemic carnitine deficiency and with CPT and LCAD deficiencies, and that differential diagnosis relies on showing long-chain urinary 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acids and measuring enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts.
quotes: long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA deficiency shares many clinical similarities with systemic carnitine deficiency, as well as with carnitine-palmityl-CoA transferase and long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiencies.

The differential diagnosis of this disease relies on the demonstration of long-chain urinary dicarboxylic acids with a hydroxyl group in 3-position and the study of the enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts.

relevance_reason: Case report of two siblings with enzymatically confirmed LCHAD deficiency, with biochemical findings and treatment outcome with MCT.

findings.statement: Duran et al. (1991) reported 2 sibs with long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency. One sib died suddenly and unexpectedly on the third day of life with extreme hypoketotic hypoglycemia. The younger sib, a girl, developed feeding problems, lowered consciousness, and liver dysfunction at age 5 months, and had signs of cardiomyopathy.
quotes: Two siblings were found to be affected by long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, one of which died suddenly and unexpectedly on the 3rd day of life suffering from extreme hypoketotic hypoglycaemia.
The younger sibling started to have feeding problems, lowered consciousness, and liver dysfunction at the age of 5 months.
signs of cardiomyopathy disappeared

findings.statement: Duran et al. (1991) found large amounts of C6-C14 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acids and conjugated 3-hydroxyoctanoic acid in the urine of the surviving patient by GC/MS, and increased plasma long-chain acylcarnitine. A phenylpropionic acid loading test revealed small but significant amounts of conjugated 3-hydroxyphenylpropionic acid in urine, and LCHAD activity was deficient in cultured skin fibroblasts.
quotes: Her urine contained large amounts of C6-C14 3-hydroxydicarboxylic acids and conjugated 3-hydroxyoctanoic acid, as verified by gas chromatography/mass spectrometry. Plasma long-chain acylcarnitine was increased.
This revealed small, but significant amounts of conjugated 3-hydroxyphenylpropionic acid (phenylhydracrylic acid) in the patient's urine.
Subsequently, the activity of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase was found to be deficient in cultured skin fibroblasts.

findings.statement: Duran et al. (1991) noted that a phenylpropionic acid loading test, which revealed urinary conjugated 3-hydroxyphenylpropionic acid (phenylhydracrylic acid), provided a clue to the diagnosis of LCHAD deficiency, subsequently confirmed by enzyme assay in fibroblasts.
quotes: A clue to the diagnosis was given by the results of a phenylpropionic acid loading test.

findings.statement: Duran et al. (1991) prescribed a diet enriched in medium-chain triglycerides based on an MCT load; on this regimen the patient thrived, signs of cardiomyopathy disappeared, and liver function normalized.
quotes: Based on the findings obtained by a medium-chain triglyceride load, a diet enriched in this type of fat was prescribed. On this regimen the patient started to thrive, signs of cardiomyopathy disappeared, and her liver function normalized.

relevance_reason: Reports two patients with LCHAD deficiency, with clinical, biochemical and enzymatic characterization and evidence for autosomal recessive inheritance.

findings.statement: Jackson et al. (1991) described 2 children with long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency who both presented with an acute metabolic crisis and hypoglycemia, and who excreted even-chain unsubstituted dicarboxylic and 3-hydroxy-dicarboxylic acids in the urine.
quotes: Both children presented with an acute metabolic crisis. Both had hypoglycemia and excreted even-chain unsubstituted dicarboxylic and 3-hydroxy-dicarboxylic acids in the urine.

findings.statement: Jackson et al. (1991) found low activity of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase but normal activity of short-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase in cultured skin fibroblasts from 2 patients; the defect was further characterized by immunoprecipitating the short-chain enzyme using monospecific antibodies.
quotes: Measurement of the enzymes of fatty acid oxidation in cultured skin fibroblasts showed low activity of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, but normal activity of short-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase.
The defect was further characterized by immunoprecipitating the short-chain enzyme using monospecific antibodies.

phenotypes.text: decreased long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity in fibroblasts

findings.statement: Jackson et al. (1991) suggested that LCHAD deficiency is probably inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, since intermediate enzyme activity was found in fibroblasts from the parents of one affected child.
quotes: It is probably inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, inasmuch as intermediate enzyme activity was found in the fibroblasts from the parents of one child.

relevance_reason: Case report of an enzymatically confirmed LCHAD-deficient patient with newly described neuropathy and retinopathy.

findings.statement: Bertini et al. (1992) described an 11-month-old girl with acute episodes of hypoglycemia and hepatic encephalopathy reminiscent of Reye syndrome, along with 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria. She had severe sensory-motor neuropathy, pigmentary retinopathy, and cardiomyopathy, and died of cardiac failure. Peripheral nerve pathology showed axonal neuropathy and demyelination. The authors noted that peripheral nerve involvement and retinal pigmentary degeneration had not been described before in patients with proven defects of mitochondrial beta-oxidation.
quotes: An 11-month-old girl presented acute episodes of hypoglycaemia and hepatic encephalopathy reminiscent of Reye syndrome and 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria.
The patient showed peculiar clinical manifestations of severe sensory-motor neuropathy, pigmentary retinopathy, and cardiomyopathy. She died of cardiac failure.
Pathological studies of peripheral nerve showed signs of axonal neuropathy and demyelination.

findings.statement: Bertini et al. (1992) found a deficiency of mitochondrial long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase in cultured fibroblasts from their patient.
quotes: Enzymatic studies in cultured fibroblasts showed a deficiency of mitochondrial long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA-dehydrogenase.

phenotypes.text: deficiency of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase in fibroblasts

relevance_reason: This paper reports a patient whose fibroblasts lacked long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity along with the long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase and thiolase activities. The authors trace this to a deficiency of the trifunctional protein. That separates combined trifunctional protein deficiency from isolated LCHAD deficiency.

findings.statement: Wanders et al. (1992) described a patient with clear signs of a mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation disorder. The patient's fibroblasts showed impaired palmitate beta-oxidation and a combined deficiency of long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, and long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase.
quotes: a patient which presented with clear manifestations of a mitochondrial beta-oxidation disorder

Subsequent studies in fibroblasts revealed an impairment in palmitate beta-oxidation and in addition, a combined deficiency of long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA-dehydrogenase and long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase.

findings.statement: Using size-exclusion chromatography, Wanders et al. (1992) showed that this patient lacked the membrane-bound multifunctional beta-oxidation enzyme protein, which carries all 3 activities. They proposed that trifunctional protein deficiency is a new disorder of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, separate from isolated deficiency of a single enzyme activity.
quotes: We show by means of size-exclusion chromatography that there is, indeed, a deficiency of the multifunctional beta-oxidation enzyme protein in this patient.
In this paper we report the identification of a new disorder of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with LCHAD deficiency combined with long-chain thiolase and hydratase deficiency (trifunctional protein deficiency), with enzyme studies in the patient and her parents.

findings.statement: Jackson et al. (1992) described a young girl who had recurrent episodes of muscle weakness that culminated in a severe attack of generalized muscle weakness.
quotes: A young girl presented with recurrent episodes of muscle weakness culminating in a severe attack of generalized muscle weakness.

findings.statement: In the patient described by Jackson et al. (1992), muscle mitochondria showed an abnormal pattern of beta-oxidation intermediates with accumulation of 3-hydroxyacyl- and 2-enoyl-CoA and carnitine esters and 3-oxoacylcarnitines. Long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase activity was low in mitochondria from all tissues, long-chain 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase activity was low in muscle mitochondria, and 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase activity with 3-oxohexadecanoyl-CoA was low in fibroblast, muscle, and cardiac mitochondria, with only partial deficiency when measured with 3-oxooctanoyl-CoA.
quotes: In the muscle mitochondria from the patient there was an abnormal pattern of intermediates of beta-oxidation with an accumulation of 3-hydroxyacyl- and 2-enoyl-CoA and carnitine esters, and 3-oxoacylcarnitines.
There was low activity of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase in mitochondria from all tissues.

The activity of long-chain 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase was low in muscle mitochondria and 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase activity measured with 3-oxohexadecanoyl-CoA as substrate was low in fibroblast, muscle, and cardiac mitochondria but only partial deficiency was present when the activity was measured with 3-oxooctanoyl-CoA.

findings.statement: Jackson et al. (1992) found that long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase activities in fibroblasts from the patient's parents were intermediate between those of controls and the patient, and concluded that the combined defect appeared to be inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
quotes: The activity of the long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase in fibroblasts from the patient's parents was intermediate between those of controls and the patient.
which appears to be inherited in an autosomal recessive manner

findings.statement: Jackson et al. (1992) concluded that the patient had a combined defect of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase, and long-chain 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase, and suggested that a multifunctional enzyme catalyzes these activities in human mitochondria and is deficient in the patient.
quotes: The patient has a combined defect of the long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, long-chain 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase, and long-chain 2-enoyl-CoA hydratase
This suggests there is a multifunctional enzyme catalyzing these activities in human mitochondria and that this enzyme is deficient in our patient.
